headline: Majors overbought and crowded long while whales rotate into cold storage; ETF bid persists but week-long exchange inflow flips to outflow.
paragraphs: The regime is overbought across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, and not one has touched a golden cross, meaning the 50-day is still below the 200-day on every major. That is a trend confirmation that stops short of acceleration. Six of seven assets are still 36 to 76 percent below their 12-month highs, with only BTC the least beaten (down 36.8 percent from 124,740). Momentum, however, is resting at the ceiling: Bitcoin RSI at 82, Ethereum at 79.1, Solana at 83.6, XRP at 80.1, BNB at 84.1. These are the readings you get after a move has already run, not the readings that precede one. MACD is above signal on all of them, which confirms the trend is still positive, but the compression between price action and overbought oscillators is the day's first structural fact. Doge and ADA are the tell: both sit below their 200-day lines even though MACD is above signal, which means the momentum indicator is not yet turning those trends around, it is early. That divergence matters.

Positioning in derivatives is expensive and tilted long. Bitcoin funding is 0.76 basis points per 8 hours, which annualizes to 8.3 percent, a normal cost for holding leverage. Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Doge are all at or above 10 annualized, with Ethereum and Solana both at 11 percent. Longs are paying to hold these bets. Open interest is dense: Bitcoin at 2.3 billion dollars, Ethereum at 1.48 billion, Solana at 268 million. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is even at 1.0, but Ethereum shows 1.18 (more longs), Solana 1.92, XRP 2.08, and Doge 3.58. Doge is the outlier: the ratio suggests the crowd is piled into longs three-and-a-half times over. Liquidations in the last 5 to 24 hours confirm the imbalance: Bitcoin saw 1,600 liquidations split nearly even, but Ethereum liquidated 11.3 million in longs against 4.8 million in shorts, Solana liquidated 5.07 million in longs against 1.01 million in shorts, and XRP liquidated 3.86 million in longs against 1.79 million in shorts. Money is being shaken out of the long side, which is crowded.

Whale flows paint a mixed picture between the two largest assets. Over the last 24 hours, 110.8 million dollars moved off exchanges in net terms, and the direction is unambiguous: 146 million in Ethereum left exchanges, while 35.2 million in Bitcoin moved back onto exchanges. The week-long trend, however, is the sharper signal. Three weeks in a row (Aug 10, Aug 17, and now the week ending Aug 24) have seen net inflows onto exchanges, with the most recent week alone recording 802 million dollars moving into Binance and OKEx. Stablecoins increased 0.02 percent over 30 days and now sit at 308.6 billion dollars, a flat float that suggests dry powder is being held but not deployed with urgency. The biggest single move in the last day was 146 million in Ethereum withdrawn from Binance to cold storage, which is a custody signal; the second was 117.7 million in Bitcoin also withdrawn from Binance. These are acts of holding, not selling.

ETF flows from traditional finance remain bid but show no acceleration. Bitcoin ETFs took in 307.5 million dollars on August 21 and 1.92 billion dollars over the last five consecutive sessions, all in the same direction (all five days positive). Ethereum ETFs saw 184 million on the same date and 692.6 million over five sessions, also all positive. Cumulative inflows are large: Bitcoin at 53.8 billion since inception, Ethereum at 12.2 billion. The pattern is steady and persistent, not frenetic. Market-wide, total cap lost 0.8 percent in 24 hours despite Bitcoin up 1.4 percent and Ethereum nearly flat, which means smaller and mid-tier coins bore the losses. Bitcoin dominance is 59.1 percent. Fear and Greed is at 73 (Greed), up from a 30-day low of 25, which places sentiment firmly in expansion but not at extremes.

The tension is structural, not directional. Majors are above their trend lines and funded long, which is textbook bullish, but RSI is crowding overbought, funding rates are normalizing upward (expensive), and the long-to-short ratios (especially Doge at 3.58 to 1) suggest crowding. Ethereum and Bitcoin are being withdrawn to cold storage, which is a patient holding signal, while smaller coins are liquidating on the long side and exchange inflows have trended positive for three straight weeks. The tape shows momentum at rest after a move, not exhaustion. Greed is real, but it is not panicked.

Watch for three shifts: first, a break below the 200-day line on Bitcoin or Ethereum; second, a funding flip on any major below 0.02 percent per 8 hours (which would signal longs have stopped paying); third, a return to net outflows off exchanges for more than two consecutive days (which would confirm holders are moving out of exchanges rather than into them). None of those conditions exist today. Until one does, the regime stays above trend with overbought momentum and mixed directional conviction from the biggest accounts.
